observations: Photo 0 shows one swivel office chair on a yellow rug in a living room.
Black fabric padded seat, black mesh backrest with a padded headrest at its top end, two adjustable armrests with silver brackets.
Chrome five-star base on castors, gas lift column.
The mesh backrest is lying flat, roughly level with the seat, so the chair is shown fully reclined or with the back folded down.
No brand name or label is readable anywhere in the photo.
The black headrest pad shows light whitish specks or marks.
Only one photo, taken from above at an angle; no upright view, no underside, no close-ups.

identity.kind: ergonomic mesh office chair with headrest and armrests

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the backrest bent back flat to the level of the seat; whether this is a recline feature or a broken back is not shown.
Age cannot be shown in a photo; no receipt shown.
Headrest pad in photo 0 shows whitish specks; no close-up of seat or headrest to tell dust from stains.
Mesh looks whole at this distance in photo 0, but there are no close-ups of mesh, seat fabric or armrest pads.
No clip of the seat being pressed and released.
Smell cannot be checked from photos.

risks.risk: Back recline mechanism or back bracket is bent or broken, so the back does not return upright or lock.
risks.proof: Clip of the back raised fully upright, locked, then sat against, then reclined and locked again.

risks.risk: Gas lift does not hold height or sinks under weight.
risks.proof: Clip of the lever raising and lowering the seat, then someone sitting for a few seconds with the height held.

risks.risk: Tears or sagging in the mesh, stains or worn foam on the seat.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the full mesh back and the seat cushion, plus a clip pressing the seat foam.
risks.if_unproven: as worn, stained seat and mesh

risks.proof: Clip moving each armrest up and down and rolling the chair across the floor.
risks.if_unproven: as needing armrest and castor repair

proof_requests: Clip of the chair back raised upright and locked, then reclined, with someone sitting in it.
Photo of the chair standing upright from the front and the side.
Clip of the gas lift raising, lowering and holding height under weight.
Close-ups of the mesh back, seat cushion and headrest showing any marks or tears.
Photo of any label under the seat showing brand or model.
response.reason: It is clearly an ergonomic mesh office chair with headrest, identified by type, and can be priced at its worst case as a damaged chair with a bent or broken back until a clip shows the back upright and locking.
